# NN20Clock partition table: # Based on the Waveshare board examples' layout
# (08_lvgl_display_panel
# 1. Their 7 MB spiffs partition is dropped: design 9 puts settings in NVS
#    and all media on the SD card
so there is nothing for an on-flash

# NN20Clock partition table: #    filesystem to hold.
# 2. Offsets are left blank so the partition tool places and aligns them.
#    The examples hardcode nvs at 0x9000
#    0x8000 partition-table offset - and our bootloader does not fit under
#    that. See CONFIG_PARTITION_TABLE_OFFSET in sdkconfig.defaults.
# 3. The single `factory` app partition became an OTA pair. The About
#    screen can update the clock over the network
#    slots plus the `otadata` the bootloader reads to decide which one to
#    run: the new image is written to the slot that is *not* running
#    only becomes the boot choice once it has been downloaded whole and
#    its SHA-256 matches what the release manifest promised.
#    There is deliberately no `factory` partition alongside them. A third
#    slot would cost 8 MB to hold an image that never changes and is
#    therefore oldest exactly when it is needed; with an OTA pair the
#    fallback is the *previous* firmware
which is a far better thing to

# NN20Clock partition table: #    land on. CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_APP_ROLLBACK_ENABLE makes that automatic:
#    an image that never reaches nn20clock_ota_mark_valid() is reverted on
#    the next boot.
#    Moving from `factory` to `ota_0` changes the offset the application
#    is flashed at
so the first build carrying this table has to go on

# NN20Clock partition table: #    over serial - see DISTRIBUTE.md. Every build after it can arrive
#    over the air.
# 8 MB per app slot is the board examples' figure and is sized for what
# lands later: LVGL
# alarm sound. Two of them plus the small data partitions come to about
# 16 MB
leaving half the flash unallocated for a media cache.

# NN20Clock partition table: # Name
nvs
otadata
phy_init
ota_0
ota_1
